  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "explanation": "stolen_card",
      "likelihood": "high",
      "reasoning": "Card/IP country mismatch combined with failed AVS supports stolen-card use. The failed id_check strengthens this explanation, although it does not establish a specific fraud mechanism."
    },
    {
      "explanation": "traveller",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Travel could explain the foreign IP and a legitimate customer could experience an AVS mismatch. However, the failed id_check prevents clearance under the policy."
    }
  ],
  "disposition": "decline",
  "citations": [
    "R03",
    "FP-2 §6.2",
    "FP-2 §6.3",
    "FP-2 §6.4",
    "FP-2 §6.6(b)",
    "FP-2 §5.3(b)",
    "FP-2 §6.5(b)",
    "FP-2 §4.2"
  ],
  "next_check": "none",
  "memo": "R03 holds: card/IP countries differ and AVS failed. Card is the only adverse family; no other rule holds, no household exception applies, and no earlier outcome settles the order. The failed id_check now decides under FP-2 §5.3(b), overriding the ordinary hold in §6.6(b). Recommend decline, not escalation, because Linkage is absent. The order is unshipped, so decline voids and refunds it and blocks the account. Travel is a plausible benign explanation for the geography, but cannot override the failed check. No further check is needed."
}
